cover.woman_bio: Born in South Carolina and raised in Harlem, she became the first Black player to win a Grand Slam title (French Open, 1956), then won Wimbledon (1957 and 1958) and the U.S. Nationals (1957 and 1958). She won 11 Grand Slam titles in all and in the early 1960s became the first Black player on the women’s professional golf tour.
cover.quote: I always wanted to be somebody.
cover.quote_source: Althea Gibson, title of her 1958 memoir (History.com; International Tennis Hall of Fame)

content.content: Exam conditions. Start your timer for 45 minutes: 5 to read and plan, 35 to write, 5 to read aloud and fix. No help button, no looking things up. Type your essay. First paragraph: a main idea sentence that picks a side. Use at least one number from EACH passage. Answer the other side once. Complete sentences; no run-ons.

Practice passages (invented for this exercise; the numbers are NOT from real studies). Should schools start later in the morning?

Passage A. In a survey of 900 students, 68% of those who started school at 9:00 a.m. said they felt awake in their first class, compared with 41% of those who started at 7:30 a.m. Students who started later also reported getting about 50 more minutes of sleep on school nights.

Passage B. A district estimates that moving the start time to 9:00 a.m. would cost QAR 400,000 a year because bus routes would have to change, and that after-school sports would end later. Supporters of the current 7:30 start say families already plan work and childcare around it.

content.content: Althea Gibson was born on August 25, 1927. She grew up in Harlem, New York, where she first fell in love with tennis. In 1950 she became the first Black player to compete at the U.S. National Championships, and in 1956 she won the French Open, the first Grand Slam title by a Black player. On July 6, 1957, she won Wimbledon, beating Darlene Hard 6–3, 6–2. She won 11 Grand Slam titles in all: five in singles and six in doubles. In the early 1960s she also became the first Black player on the women’s professional golf tour. Her 1958 memoir was titled I Always Wanted to Be Somebody.
